title: Builder Signals · 2026-06-29
summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 25 条 X 动态、1 集播客、1 篇博客；本站精选 9 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Swyx · AI Engineer 大会主理人、Latent Space 主播
featured.summaryEn: Swyx argues that if you take Noam's point about keeping a constant inference budget for evals seriously, open models have far more dollar-per-token mileage than closed model APIs. So anyone launching an open model—or situationally incentivized toward open—should report thinking levels measured by dollar inference on popular providers, instead of token counts on the x-axis. It's a quiet push to reframe how the field benchmarks cost-effectiveness.
featured.insightZh: Swyx 借着 Noam（OpenAI）"评测应固定推理预算"的说法引出一个有意思的角度：开源模型在每美元能买到的 token 数上，比闭源模型 API 划算得多。所以他主张，任何今天发布开源模型、或在场景上倾向开源的团队，理应用"在主流推理服务商上每美元能跑多少推理"来标注思考档位（thinking levels），而不是简单地把 token 数画在横轴上。这其实是在重新定义大家怎么公平地比较模型的"性价比"。

featured.title: Thibault Sottiaux · OpenAI Codex 与 ChatGPT 负责人
featured.summaryEn: OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT lead Thibault Sottiaux shipped a batch of Codex improvements: smoother handling of super-long threads, a hoverable navigation rail for previewing and jumping between turns, broader settings search with clearer appearance and host-filtering controls, fixed tooltip/menu/autocomplete misalignment on zoom, and Slack copy that now preserves Markdown without freezing the UI on large pastes. And "most importantly," per him, a dedicated Pets panel—the half-joking headline that pulled over a thousa…
featured.insightZh: OpenAI 的 Codex 与 ChatGPT 负责人 Thibault Sottiaux 列了一波 Codex 刚落地的改进：超长会话线程处理更顺滑；新增可悬停的导航栏，方便在不同回合之间预览和跳转；设置搜索覆盖更多控制项，外观和主机过滤选项更清晰，自定义 provider 设置更好找；缩放级别不再让提示框、对话框、菜单、选择气泡、拖拽预览和自动补全错位；复制到 Slack 时能保留 Markdown 格式（项目符号、加粗、代码、链接），大段文本粘贴也不再卡 UI。当然，他自己强调"最重要的"是新增了一个专门的宠物面板（Pets panel）——这条带玩笑性质的发布吸引了上千点赞。

featured.title: Memory and Continual Learning：Engram 的 Dan Biderman 与 Jessy Lin
featured.summaryEn: Models don't lack raw intelligence—they lack the ability to bake new, evolving context deeply into their weights, which is exactly the continual learning Engram is building. Engram cofounders Dan Biderman (a neuroscientist) and Jessy Lin argue the bottleneck to more useful models isn't raw intelligence but understanding new, evolving context. Rather than treating memory as an external database or context-window stuffing, they use the same training pipeline frontier labs use for math and code—SFT, RL, on-policy distillation, and adapter/LoRA fine-tuning—to train each company's or team's private context directly into weights. The result is "a model per team" that understands your way of doing things like a multi-year employee, without rereading files. Their most counterintuitive figure: internalizing this into weights can yield a two-orders-of-magnitude reduction in inference token consum…
featured.insightZh: 模型不缺原始智能，缺的是把"新的、不断演化的上下文"真正烧进权重里的能力——而这正是 Engram 在做的"持续学习"。 Engram 的两位联合创始人 Dan Biderman（神经科学背景）和 Jessy Lin 认为，今天阻碍模型变得更有用的瓶颈，不是原始智能，而是理解新的、不断变化的上下文。他们不把记忆看成外挂的数据库或塞进上下文窗口的东西，而是用前沿实验室训练模型攻克数学、代码的同一套流程（监督微调、RL、on-policy distillation、各类 adapter / LoRA 微调），把每个公司、每个团队的专属上下文直接训练进权重里——做出"每个团队一个模型"，让模型像在公司干了多年的老员工一样，不用反复读文件就懂你们的做事方式。 他们给出的最反直觉的数字是：把这些东西内化进权重，可以带来"两个数量级"的推理 token 消耗下降。Jessy Lin 的原话是——很多与人、团队、组织、优先级相关的东西"模型可以隐式学会，用 100 个 token 就回答，而最好的前沿模型要烧 10 万个 token 才做到"。他们称之为某种"RAG killer"：不是说不能再检索，而是很多高频、重复、与组织语境强相关的任务，可以靠轻量训练变成模型的"本能"，不必每次都跑冗长的检索循环。 更深一层，他们把这件事类比成人脑——什么该内化进"神经组织"、什么该写下来外置，是一个尚未解决的根本问题；他们刻意少用启发式过滤，因为人类"刷了很多垃圾信息大脑也不会跑偏"。终局愿景是：每个人、每个团队都有一个和前沿模型不同的、真正属于自己的模型，你在工作中投入越多，模型在你关心的领域表现就越好。

items.title: Peter Yang · AI 实用教程创作者
items.summaryEn: AI tutorials creator Peter Yang shared two things. First, his health automation: every Saturday Hermes emails him a health check with takeaways and stats, pulling from his Withings smart scale API, Fitbit, Google Health, and a vibe-coded MCP server plus fitness app he built to track workouts—useful even as his body fat trends the wrong way. Second, a pushback on a problem-escalation framework: if you wait until "level 5" to flag an issue when the fire has burned for days and your "fix" didn't actually fix anything…
items.insightZh: AI 实用教程创作者 Peter Yang 这周分享了两件事。一是他自己搭的健康自动化：每周六让 Hermes 给他发一封健康体检邮件，汇总要点和数据——数据来自 Withings 智能秤的 API、Fitbit 和 Google Health、以及他自己 vibe-code 出来的一个 MCP server 加健身记录 app。他说哪怕体脂在往错误方向走，这套东西也很有用。二是他对某个"问题升级分级框架"的反驳：如果你非要等到 level 5 才告诉别人有问题，而火已经烧了好几天、你的"解决方案"其实根本没修好，那你的处境一定比 level 1、第一时间就把问题说出来一起找解法的人更糟。他强调这类事没有非黑即白，都有 nuance。

items.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
items.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch raised a security flag: Mythos / Sol cybersecurity capabilities are equally useful offensively and defensively. If adversaries get hold of an equivalent offensive capability, it's a serious threat to US companies still unaware of latent vulnerabilities. In the meantime, he strongly recommends running deepsec or similar harnesses with available frontier models to self-audit. A rare, blunt take on how frontier-model offensive capability cuts both ways.
items.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 抛出一个安全警示：Mythos / Sol 这类网络安全能力，攻防两面同样好用。如果对手拿到了等价的进攻型能力，那对那些还没意识到自己存在潜在漏洞的美国公司来说，是个实打实的威胁。在此之前，他强烈建议用 deepsec 之类的 harness 配合现有前沿模型，主动去跑一遍自查。这是少见地把"前沿模型的攻击能力会反过来威胁防御方"这件事讲得很直白的一条。

items.title: Aaron Levie · Box CEO
items.summaryEn: Box CEO Aaron Levie's take on AI token cost optimization: the best practices are good, but none of it works without a deep, non-abstract understanding of the underlying work. The implication—a layer between the work itself and the underlying intelligence must deeply understand your workflows, context, and business processes. Each company doing this alone won't scale, so this is effectively the playbook for every applied AI company: eval models for the use case, master the domain, tune UX and features, and support…
items.insightZh: Box CEO Aaron Levie 就"AI token 成本优化"给出了他的判断：这些最佳实践本身不错，但前提是你得非抽象地、深入地理解底层正在做的工作。最终的含义是——在"工作本身"和"底层智能"之间，需要有一层东西去深刻理解你的工作流、上下文和业务流程。而每家公司各自单干，很难规模化做好，所以这事实上就是当下所有应用层 AI 公司的剧本：通过针对应用场景做模型评测、吃透领域、为具体用例打磨 UX 和功能、再靠 FDE（前向部署工程师）支撑落地和变革，这一层就能创造巨大价值。结果是企业拿到更高 ROI——因为靠最优的架构和工作流，你其实能用每一美元换到"更多"智能。他认为横向和纵向都会有很多版本，是当下的巨大机会。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder、Follow Builders 作者
items.summaryEn: Follow Builders author Zara Zhang shared a number that captures the year: she barely knew how GitHub worked a year ago, and now has 10k GitHub followers—while still not writing code by hand. She clarifies she's not an engineer; these are side projects built for fun. What she loves is connecting technology to real user pain points, using it to solve her own, and then telling the products' stories. The self-portrait of building influence through vibe coding rather than hand-written code pulled 2,000+ likes—a snapsho…
items.insightZh: Follow Builders 的作者 Zara Zhang 晒了一组很能说明这一年变化的数字：去年她还几乎不懂 GitHub 怎么用，现在 GitHub 上已经有 1 万关注者——而她到现在仍然不会手写代码。她补充说自己其实不是工程师，这些都是为了好玩做的 side project；她真正热爱的是把技术和用户的真实痛点连起来、用来解决自己的痛点，然后把这些产品的故事讲出来。这条"不会手写代码却靠 vibe coding 积累出影响力"的自述拿到了 2000 多点赞，本身就是当下 builder 生态的一个缩影。

items.title: Matt Turck · FirstMark 风投合伙人、MAD Podcast 主播
items.summaryEn: FirstMark VC and MAD Podcast host Matt Turck riffed a short "history of smart glasses," skewering the category's decade of awkwardness: Google 2013 ("you really want this"—no), Microsoft 2016 (enterprise—"maybe, but no"), Meta 2023 (normal-looking with AI—"wait, maybe… actually no"), Apple 2024 ($3,499 covering your whole face—"absolutely not"), and Snap 2026 ("this time for real"—"we admire the persistence but still no"). A light jab that doubles as commentary on a hardware category's repeated misfires.
items.insightZh: FirstMark 风投合伙人、MAD Podcast 主播 Matt Turck 用一段简短的"智能眼镜简史"调侃了这个品类十几年的尴尬：2013 年 Google 说"你真的想要这个"，所有人说"不想"；2016 年微软说"那如果是给企业用呢"，企业说"也许吧，但还是不"；2023 年 Meta 说"那如果它看起来正常、还带 AI 呢"，大家说"等等……也许？……其实还是不"；2024 年 Apple 说"那如果它卖 3499 美元、还盖住你整张脸呢"，大家说"绝对不行"；到 2026 年 Snap 说"这次来真的"，大家说"我们佩服你的执着，但仍然不"。一段轻松的吐槽，背后是对硬件品类反复试错的观察。

items.title: Claude Code now supports artifacts
items.summaryEn: Claude Code can now capture work progress as an artifact—a shareable, visual web page that updates itself as the session works. A session ranging from incident investigation to service refactoring to months of data analysis becomes a page anyone can open: a PR walkthrough, a filterable dashboard, or a release checklist that fills itself out. Crucially it's built from the session's full context—your codebase, connectors, and conversation—so "you ask for a page, and Claude Code builds it from what already exists," no wiring data sources or standing up infrastructure. Every publish is a new version at the same link with version history for rollback, and open pages refresh in place so teammates see updates instantly. Their most common internal use is debugging: an engineer kicks off an incident investigation before standup, and Claude Code publishes an artifact—timeline, suspect commits, er…
items.insightZh: Claude Code 现在能把工作进展捕捉成 artifact——一个会随会话自动更新的、可分享的可视化网页。一次 Claude Code 会话可以从排查线上故障、重构服务到分析数月数据，artifact 会把这些工作转成任何人都能打开探索的网页：PR 走查、可筛选可排序的看板、甚至会随工作自动勾选的发布清单。关键是它用的是会话的完整上下文——你的代码库、连接器和对话本身，所以你不用自己接数据源或搭基础设施，"你只要请求一个页面，Claude Code 就用已有的东西把它建出来"。每次发布都是同一链接下的新版本，带版本历史可随时回滚，更新后页面会原地刷新、队友立刻看到最新状态。他们内部最常见的用例是 debug：工程师在站会前发起故障调查，Claude Code 边查边发布带时间线、可疑 commit 和错误率图表的 artifact，到站会时已自动重发了两版。目前 artifact 以 beta 形式向 Claude Team 和 Enterprise 组织开放，默认仅作者可见、只能在组织内分享、无法公开，管理员可通过 org 级开关和合规 API 管控访问与留存。
